title: Best Travel Laundry Detergent 2026: 5 Options
description: Sea to Summit Trek & Travel, Tide Pods travel size, Ecover Zero, all Free Clear Mighty Pacs and the Scrubba wash bag combo — compared on TSA liquid rules, cold-water washing and cost per load.
lede: The wrong detergent leaks through your toiletry bag at 35,000 feet. This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: How We Compared 5 Travel Detergents
paragraphs: Travel laundry is a niche category with real trade-offs. A liquid that doubles as body wash saves bag space but risks spillage. Pods are foolproof for hotel machines but useless for sink washing. A wash bag system is the most self-sufficient option — but costs three times as much as a bottle of detergent.

| Product | Price | Key Strength | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sea to Summit Trek & Travel | $8–$12 / 3 oz | Multi-use liquid | Best all-rounder |
| Tide Pods Travel Size | $10–$15 / 10 ct | Zero-mess pods | Best for hotel machines |
| Ecover Zero (Small) | $15–$20 / 16 oz | Plant-based, fragrance-free | Best eco pick |
| all Free Clear Mighty Pacs | $8–$12 / 10 ct | Hypoallergenic pods | Best for sensitive skin |
| Scrubba Wash Bag + Detergent | $60–$80 combo | Portable washboard system | Best off-grid |

One note on ratings: if you fly with carry-on only and want zero checked luggage, Sea to Summit and the pod options (Tide, all) are the cleanest choices. The Scrubba combo is bulkier but makes you completely independent of laundromats and hotel facilities.

sections.heading: Sea to Summit Trek & Travel Liquid Wash — Best All-Rounder
paragraphs: The 3 oz (89 ml) bottle passes TSA liquid rules without decanting. One cap-full — roughly 7 ml — cleans a full load in a hotel sink or handles a dirty hiking shirt after a long day. Travelers report one bottle covering an 18-day trip through Southeast Asia with roughly 30% left on return.

The soap is genuinely concentrated. It lathers with cold water, rinses quickly without leaving residue, and the biodegradable formula is safe for grey-water disposal at campsites. Travelers report using it as body wash when shower gel runs out mid-trip, with no skin irritation from daily use.

The downside is that it's liquid. The flip-top cap does not lock, and a cap popping open inside a packed bag is a recurring complaint in traveller reviews. The solution is to pack it inside a zip-lock. At $8–$12 for a 3 oz bottle, it's also not cheap per ml compared to buying a travel-size generic at a pharmacy abroad.

sections.heading: Tide Pods Travel Size — Best for Hotel Laundry Machines
paragraphs: A pack of 10 Tide Pods runs $10–$15 and handles 10 machine loads — roughly $1–$1.50 per wash. The pre-measured pod format means no measuring, no spilling, and no guessing whether the hotel machine takes powder or liquid. Drop one pod in, close the door, done.

Cleaning power is Tide's flagship formula in a compact package. Cotton shirts, denim, and synthetic workout gear all come out clean in user reports. The pods dissolve reliably at 30°C and above, with undissolved residue rarely mentioned.

Pods have a structural weakness: they're useless for hand-washing in a sink. The pod casing doesn't break down in small volumes of cold water the way liquid soap does. If your accommodation has no laundry machine — hostels with hand-wash sinks, Airbnbs, trekking lodges — Tide Pods won't help you. They're also single-use plastic, which matters if you're trying to reduce packaging waste.

sections.heading: Ecover Zero Laundry Detergent — Best Eco Pick
paragraphs: Ecover Zero is 100% plant-based, fragrance-free, and holds the EU Ecolabel certification. The 16 oz bottle ($15–$20) is larger than the Sea to Summit option, which means it's less suited for carry-on-only travel — but it's the right call for checked luggage or a slow-travel itinerary where you're staying weeks at a time in one place.

The formula is genuinely fragrance-free, not just 'lightly scented.' For travelers who react to synthetic perfumes — or who simply don't want their clothes smelling like lavender in a humid climate — this is the standout feature. It also works well in cold water, important in countries where hot water in hostel laundry rooms is not guaranteed.

The larger bottle is both a strength and a limitation. You get roughly 25–30 hand-wash loads from 16 oz, which is excellent value, but the bottle itself is heavy and awkward to split into a smaller travel container without a funnel. Ecover doesn't sell a dedicated travel-size SKU in most markets, so you're decanting yourself.

sections.heading: all Free Clear Mighty Pacs — Best for Sensitive Skin
paragraphs: all Free Clear is the dermatologist-recommended option. The formula contains no dyes, no perfumes, and has been approved by the National Psoriasis Foundation. For travelers who deal with eczema, contact dermatitis, or simply prefer to avoid synthetic additives, these pods are the safest machine-wash option in this comparison.

Pricing sits at $8–$12 for a 10-count travel pack — nearly identical to Tide Pods. Cleaning performance is solid on everyday fabrics. It's not the strongest detergent for heavily soiled items (think mud-caked hiking socks), but for the typical travel load of shirts, underwear, and light pants, it cleans reliably at 30–40°C.

Like Tide Pods, all Free Clear Mighty Pacs are machine-only. They don't dissolve in sink water. The pod format also adds single-use plastic packaging. If your primary concern is skin sensitivity and you have access to a washing machine, these are the best pods in this lineup — but if you hand-wash frequently, you need a liquid instead.

sections.heading: Scrubba Wash Bag + Detergent Combo — Best Off-Grid
paragraphs: The Scrubba Wash Bag is a dry bag with an internal flexible washboard — a grid of rubber nobbles on the interior lining. Fill it with water, add a small amount of detergent (included in the combo), seal the valve, and knead the bag against your clothes for 3 minutes. The washboard creates friction that replaces the agitation drum of a washing machine.

It genuinely works. Cotton socks and synthetic baselayers came out clean after a 3-minute scrub. The bag dries fast and doubles as a dry bag for electronics. The included detergent sachets (usually 3–5 in the combo) are enough for the trip duration; after that, you refill with any liquid detergent.

The price — $60–$80 for the combo — is the main barrier. That's 5–8x the cost of a bottle of Sea to Summit or a pack of pods. You're paying for the wash bag itself, which lasts years. The weight penalty is also real: the Scrubba adds about 140 g (5 oz) to your pack. For ultralight travelers, that's a meaningful cost. If you routinely travel off-grid for 7+ days, the Scrubba pays for itself quickly in laundromat savings. For weekend trips or city travel with machine access, it's overkill.

sections.heading: Choosing by Trip Type
paragraphs: Carry-on only, city travel: Sea to Summit Trek & Travel or Tide Pods. Both pass TSA rules, take up minimal space, and handle hotel machine or sink scenarios respectively. Sea to Summit wins if you mix hand-wash and machine-wash. Tide Pods win if you only use hotel machines and want zero mess.

Sensitive skin or eco-conscious travel: all Free Clear Mighty Pacs for sensitive skin with machine access, Ecover Zero for eco-conscious travelers willing to check luggage or use a larger bottle for longer stays.

Camping, hiking, off-grid: Scrubba Wash Bag combo is the only self-sufficient option. Pair it with Sea to Summit liquid after the included sachets run out — Sea to Summit is designed for the Scrubba workflow and produces minimal suds that rinse fast.

faqs.q: Can I bring liquid laundry detergent on a plane?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the container is 3.4 oz (100 ml) or smaller and fits in your quart-size liquids bag. Sea to Summit Trek & Travel comes in a TSA-compliant 3 oz bottle. Pods (Tide, all Free Clear) are solid and have no liquid restriction.

faqs.q: Which travel detergent works best for hand-washing?
faqs.a: Sea to Summit Trek & Travel Liquid Wash is the best hand-wash option. It's concentrated, lathers in cold water, and rinses quickly without leaving residue. Pods do not dissolve reliably in sink water and are not suitable for hand-washing.

faqs.q: Is the Scrubba Wash Bag worth it for short trips?
faqs.a: Probably not for trips under 7 days with access to hotel or laundromat machines. At $60–$80, it makes most sense for multi-week off-grid trips, hiking expeditions, or travelers who consistently stay in places without laundry facilities.

faqs.q: What's the most eco-friendly travel detergent?
faqs.a: Ecover Zero holds the EU Ecolabel and is 100% plant-based and biodegradable. Sea to Summit is also biodegradable and marketed specifically for backcountry use where grey-water impact matters. Both are better than conventional pods, which add single-use plastic packaging.

faqs.q: Which detergent is best for sensitive skin?
faqs.a: all Free Clear Mighty Pacs are formulated without dyes or perfumes and are approved by the National Psoriasis Foundation. For hand-washing, Ecover Zero is also fragrance-free and gentler than most travel liquids.

faqs.q: How many washes do I get from a 3 oz bottle of Sea to Summit?
faqs.a: Approximately 18–25 washes depending on load size and whether you're hand-washing small items or filling a sink. One cap-full (about 7 ml) handles a sink full of clothes. A 3 oz (89 ml) bottle gives roughly 12 full-sink washes or more loads for smaller items.

faqs.q: Can Tide Pods be used in cold water?
faqs.a: Tide Pods are designed to dissolve in 60°F (15°C) water and above, including cold cycles. However, in very cold water — under 60°F — dissolution can be incomplete. In most hotel and laundromat machines, you will not encounter this issue.

faqs.q: Is travel laundry detergent safe for delicates and merino wool?
faqs.a: Sea to Summit and Ecover Zero are both safe for merino wool and synthetics. Tide Pods and all Free Clear pods can be used on delicates but check the care label — some merino items require a wool-specific wash. The Scrubba's mechanical scrubbing action is rougher and should be used gently on delicate fabrics.

faqs.q: How long do the Scrubba included detergent sachets last?
faqs.a: The Scrubba combo typically includes 3–5 single-use sachets, enough for a 5–7 day trip. After that, refill with any liquid detergent — Sea to Summit is a popular pairing. Use only a small amount (5 ml or less) since excess suds are hard to rinse from the sealed bag.

faqs.q: Where can I buy travel-size laundry detergent abroad?
faqs.a: Supermarkets and pharmacies in most countries sell travel-size or sachet detergent. In Southeast Asia and Japan, single-use laundry sachets are widely available for 10–30 cents each. Bringing your own is most useful on the first few days before you can locate a local shop, or in remote areas with no stores.

offerNotes.sea-to-summit-trek-travel-wash: Concentrated biodegradable liquid, doubles as body wash, TSA-compliant 3 oz — the most versatile single bottle for multi-week carry-on travel.
offerNotes.tide-pods-travel-size: Pre-measured, no-spill pods with Tide's full cleaning formula — best drop-in solution for hotel and laundromat machines.
offerNotes.ecover-zero-laundry-detergent: EU Ecolabel certified, 100% plant-based and fragrance-free — ideal for eco-conscious travelers or anyone sensitive to synthetic scents.
offerNotes.all-laundry-detergent-pods: Dye-free and perfume-free pods approved by the National Psoriasis Foundation — the safest pod option for eczema-prone or sensitive skin.
offerNotes.scrubba-wash-bag-detergent: Portable washboard bag plus detergent sachets; makes you fully independent of laundromats for off-grid trips of 7+ days.

pinDescription: Five travel laundry detergents compared: Sea to Summit Trek & Travel, Tide Pods, Ecover Zero, all Free Clear and the Scrubba wash bag. Which survive a carry-on, sink washing and off-grid camping? #travelhacks
